rows: A trained spotter at a petroleum plant in rural Crane county reported 60 mph wind gusts. No damage was reported.
Penny size hail fell two miles north of Tubbs Corner in western Crane County on Farm to Market Road 1053.
Golfball to baseball size hail fell along U.S. Highway 385 north of Crane.
Nickel size hail fell at the intersection of Farm to Market Roads 1053 and 1233.
Penny size hail was reported on Farm to Market Road 1601 northwest of Crane.
Marble to golfball size hail fell along U.S. Highway 385 north of Crane.
Quarter to golfball size hail fell in a swath south of Crane.
Trained spotters from the Chevron-Warren Petroleum Plant estimated 60 mph winds. No damage was reported.
Penny to nickel sized hail fell at the Chevron--Warren Petroleum plant and along Texas State Highway 1053.
Local law enforcement relayed a trained spotter report of a tornado west of Crane. No damage was reported.
Quarter to golfball sized hail fell in Crane.
A trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail about 13 miles northwest of Imperial. About 25 minutes later, the same spotter reported quarter sized hail 17 miles north of Imperial.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail falling at the intersection of FM1601 & FM1233.
A thunderstorm moved over Crane County and produced a wind gust of 65 mph four miles west of Crane.
A thunderstorm moved over Crane and produced wind damage. Utility poles were snapped inside the city limits of Crane along Highway 385. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Crane County and produced baseball sized hail in Crane. A damage survey was conducted the next day. Many vehicles had hail damage ranging from broken windshields to numerous dents. The majority of the damage was to vehicles, however there was damage no…
A thunderstorm moved across Crane County and produced one inch hail in Roadside Park south of Crane on Highway 385.

A thunderstorm moved across Crane County and produced golf ball sized hail south of Crane on Highway 385. There were reports of broken windows and some damage to cars. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Crane County and produced wind damage in the City of Crane. There were downed powerlines at W. 6th Street and Katherine Street. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Crane County and produced a 62 mph wind gust one mile north northwest of Crane.
A thunderstorm moved across Crane County and produced a 64 mph wind gust one mile north northwest of Crane at the Mesonet site.
A thunderstorm produced ping pong to two inch hail stones near Crane, TX.
A thunderstorm produced a 65 mph wind gust five miles west of Crane.
A thunderstorm produced a 61 mph wind gust ten miles south of Penwell.
A thunderstorm produced a 58 mph wind gust near Crane at the mesonet site.
A thunderstorm produced a 69 mph wind gust at the Crane Mesonet site.
Public report of pea to ping pong ball size hail between Grandfalls and Crane. Time and location are estimated from radar.
A report from the public of tennis ball-size hail in Crane was shared on social media.
The West Texas Mesonet station 1 NNW Crane measured a 64 mph wind gust.
The West Texas Mesonet station at Crane measured a 65 mph wind gust. The sheriff's office in Crane relayed a delayed report of some power outages, but did not reported any damage.
